page: Amazon Web Services x8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the ARM64-based AWS Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz, this instance features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the server's strong memory subsystem and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 368.85 GB/sec for read operations and 186.53 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core processing is robust, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 23349.0 and a strong stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 81892.57. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the top tier, with web serving reaching 102.03 GB/sec. However, single-core performance and small-model text generation remain average to weak, indicating that workloads must be parallelized to leverage the hardware fully.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x8g.12xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high memory density and strong multi-threaded throughput without the premium associated with traditional x86 memory-optimized instances. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a highly specialized option for memory-bound, non-graphical workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
